heading: Window controls need permission
body: client/manifest.json declares the window that a native target opens and the controls that a service may use, under `tac.application.window.controls`. By default, the manifest grants nothing. A service gets the controls by injection, like the other browser APIs: `@Needs windowControls` in JavaScript and TypeScript, and a `WindowControls` field in every language that runs in the page. A service that the native app links in (Rust and C# on the desktop, Swift on Apple, Kotlin on Android) has no page, so the build refuses `WindowControls` there (`TY1317`), and F# services have no browser APIs yet. A service never reads `globalThis` (`TY1360`). `granted(control)` answers whether a control is granted; ask it before you offer a control. A call to a control that is not granted fails at once, and the message names the grant to add. In a browser tab nothing is granted, because the page has no native window. The host checks the manifest grants again before it runs a request. A test unit fakes the controls like any browser API: a `@Fake windowControls` field in JavaScript and TypeScript, and `BrowserFakes` in Go, Ruby and Swift. These controls do not sandbox (restrict) the native service code that the application owns. That code runs with the operating system permissions of the host process. See the feature "What a page may do to its window" for the service in every language.
